arxiv-2105-04298.title: Nucleation of laboratory earthquakes: quantitative analysis and scalings
arxiv-2105-04298.creator: Manuscript submitted to J. Geophys. Res.
arxiv-2105-04298.description: Abstract Decades of seismological observations have highlighted the variability of foreshock occurrence prior to natural earthquakes, making thus difficult to track how earthquakes start. Here, we report on three stick-slip experiments performed on cylindrical samples of Indian metagabbro under upper crustal stress conditions (30-60 MPa ). Acoustic emissions (AEs) were continuously recorded by 8 calibrated acoustic sensors during the experiments.

arxiv-2312-16714.title: A Reversible Perspective on Petri Nets and Event Structures DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX CCS: Theory of computation Concurrency CCS: Theory of computation Operational semantics
arxiv-2312-16714.creator: Hernán Melgratti, Claudio Antares Mezzina, G. Michele Pinna
arxiv-2312-16714.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Hernán Melgratti, Claudio Antares Mezzina, G. Michele Pinna. Event structures have emerged as a foundational model for concurrent computation, explaining computational processes by outlining the events and the relationships that dictate their execution. They play a pivotal role in the study of key aspects of concurrent computation models, such as causality and independence, and have found applications across a broad range of languages and models, spanning realms like persistence, probabilities, and quantum computing.

arxiv-2409-11806.title: Exotic Dehn twists and homotopy coherent group actions
arxiv-2409-11806.creator: Sungkyung Kang, JungHwan Park, Masaki Taniguchi
arxiv-2409-11806.description: Abstract . We consider the question of extending a smooth homotopy coherent finite cyclic group action on the boundary of a smooth 4-manifold to its interior. As a result, we prove that Dehn twists along any Seifert homology sphere, except the 3-sphere, on their simply connected positive-definite fillings are infinite order exotic. 1.

arxiv-2410-18274.title: Electromagnetic follow-up of gravitational waves: review and lessons learned
arxiv-2410-18274.creator: M. Nicholl 1 and I. Andreoni 2,3,4
arxiv-2410-18274.description: Abstract The detection of gravitational waves (GWs) has provided a new tool to study the Universe, with the scientific return enriched when combined with established probes: electromagnetic (EM) radiation and energetic particles. Since the groundbreaking detection in 2017 of merging neutron stars producing GW emission, a gamma-ray burst and an optical ‘kilonova’, the field has grown rapidly.

arxiv-2504-18166.title: Quantifying quantum-state texture
arxiv-2504-18166.creator: Yiding Wang, Hui Liu, and Tinggui Zhang †
arxiv-2504-18166.description: Abstract Quantum-state texture is a newly recognized quantum resource that has garnered attention with the advancement of quantum theory. In this work, we introduce several potential quantum-state texture measure schemes and check whether they satisfy the three fundamental conditions required for a valid quantum-state texture measure.

arxiv-2509-13557.title: MALTA: An Automated CGRA Design Framework
arxiv-2509-13557.creator: Zesong Jiang, Yuqi Sun, Qing Zhong, Mahathi Krishna, Deepak Patil, Cheng Tan, Sriram Krishnamoorthy, Jeff Zhang
arxiv-2509-13557.description: Abstract Coarse-grained Reconfigurable Arrays (CGRAs) are a promising computing architecture that can deliver high-performance, energy-efficient acceleration across diverse domains. By supporting reconfiguration at the functional unit level, CGRAs efficiently adapt to varying computational patterns and optimize resource utilization. However, designing CGRAs is highly challenging due to the vast design space, independent architectural parameters, and the time-consuming nature of manual design.

pmc-11434762.description: Quorum sensing (QS) is a mechanism by which bacteria detect and respond to cell density, regulating collective behaviors.
